definition: Every active county indicator receives a constituency and ward disposition; published child data are counted from canonical series and never inferred from parent values.

rows.disposition_reason: Agriculture share of GCP requires a constituency agriculture numerator and constituency GCP denominator on the same accounting basis. Neither is published for the current 290 constituencies, so the county share cannot be inherited.
Agriculture share of GCP requires matched ward numerator and denominator economic accounts. Those are not published in the governed source, and the county percentage cannot be copied downward.

Agriculture GVA is sourced from county economic accounts. The source does not publish current electoral-constituency GVA, and no governed small-area production model has been approved for deterministic disaggregation.
Agriculture GVA is a county-accounting measure in the governed source. Ward values cannot be inferred by land area, population or equal allocation without fabricating local output.

The canonical Class C rural-road total is published by KNBS on a county basis. No official current-290 constituency allocation is published in that source, and the Atlas has no approved authoritative Class C road-line spatial derivation that can reproduce the county accounting total without introducing boundary or network-classification error.

The governed Class C road-length source publishes county totals, not ward totals. Without an approved authoritative Class C road-line dataset and deterministic boundary intersection/reconciliation pipeline, county kilometres cannot be inherited, divided, or estimated for wards.

The canonical 2023/24 Kenya Housing Survey computer-use measure is not published in the Atlas as a valid ward-domain estimate. Copying or allocating the county percentage to wards would create false precision and is prohibited.

Modern contraceptive use is a survey estimate whose published domain is county. No valid official ward estimate is available; county values cannot be copied or proportionally allocated to wards.

The canonical value is KNBS's 2019 KPHC Analytical Report on Disability, Table 2.13, published directly for all 47 counties only. The Washington Group Short Set disability estimate is not tabulated below county in that report, and no current-290-constituency table or administrative-unit crosswalk exists, so the county figure cannot be inherited or recomputed for constituencies.

KNBS's 2019 KPHC Analytical Report on Disability, Table 2.13 is a county-only table. Since the source does not reach even the current 290 constituencies (see the constituency-level closure for this indicator), it self-evidently does not reach the finer 1,450-ward geography, and no ward-domain disability estimate or crosswalk exists.

IND-ELECTRICITY-ACCESS is a governed P20 profile-slot alias of the already-published KNBS 2023/24 Kenya Housing Survey Table 5.11 main-grid-electricity observation (identical source table, series and value basis as IND-MAIN-GRID-ELECTRICITY, which is already closed governed_unavailable at constituency level). The underlying KHS is a county-domain household survey; no compatible constituency-domain estimate is published, so this alias inherits the identical closure rather than being independently re-derived or copied downward.

As the P20 alias of IND-MAIN-GRID-ELECTRICITY (identical KHS Table 5.11 source, already closed governed_unavailable at ward level), this indicator carries the same ward-domain publication gap: the 2023/24 Kenya Housing Survey is not designed as a ward-domain estimate and no compatible ward table or crosswalk exists.

The canonical FGM measure is a sensitive KDHS county-domain estimate with ranking withheld. No official current-constituency estimate with valid survey precision is published, so local downscaling is prohibited.

The canonical FGM measure is not a ward-domain estimate. Inheriting or modelling the county percentage at ward level without an approved survey-domain method would create false precision for a sensitive indicator.

EPRA's monthly maximum retail petroleum price order gazettes prices only for a limited set of representative marketing towns (the Atlas already uses one representative town per county, e.g. Kitale for Trans Nzoia, explicitly flagged in the observation notes as 'not a county average'). EPRA does not gazette a price for each of the 290 constituencies, and most constituencies contain no gazetted pricing town at all, so assigning the county's representative-town price to every constituency in it (or to any other constituency) would fabricate constituency-level precision the regulator itself does not publish.

The same EPRA representative-town pricing gap that prevents constituency-level publication applies a fortiori at ward level: EPRA gazettes far fewer pricing towns than the 1,450 current wards, so no defensible ward assignment exists without fabricating precision the regulator does not publish.

KNBS Gross County Product is an official county economic-accounting product. No compatible official current-290 constituency GCP allocation is published, and allocating county GCP by population, land area or equal shares would manufacture local economic output.
KNBS Gross County Product is published at county level. No official ward GCP allocation exists in the governed source, and parent GCP cannot be divided or inherited to wards.

rows.indicator_name: Health facilities assessed in the 2023 Health Facility Census
rows.disposition_reason: The canonical Atlas indicator is the dated August-September 2023 Ministry of Health Health Facility Census assessment count (data/p20/source/health-facility-density-2023.json), reviewed for child-domain feasibility in data/p23x/health-facility-child-domain-review.json. The live KMHFR registry exposes constituency-labelled facility records but is a current/live system, not the fixed 2023 census-assessment universe, and substituting a live registry count for the dated census count would misstate the indicator. No official dated facility-level 2023 census extract or child-domain tabulation has yet been located, so no defensible constituency value can be produced without first resolving the open source-semantics reconciliation (14,883 vs 12,384 facilities) recorded in that review.

rows.indicator_name: Health facilities assessed in the 2023 Health Facility Census
rows.disposition_reason: As at constituency level, the canonical 2023 Health Facility Census assessment count has no dated facility-level extract or official ward tabulation available, and a live KMHFR registry count cannot be substituted for the fixed dated census universe without misstating the indicator, per data/p23x/health-facility-child-domain-review.json.

Closed under data/p23/constituency-evidence-gap-closure-contract.json: KMHFR can support constituency facility counts, but no authoritative current-290-constituency population denominator aligned to the facility reference period is publicly available, so a facilities-per-10,000-residents rate cannot be derived. No county population is inherited downward.

Closed under data/p24/ward-health-facility-density-closure-contract.json after a genuine spatial_derivation attempt: KMHFR (the designated source) was unreachable from the build environment on repeated attempts; the only official KMHFR-derived extract obtainable (HDX 2017 snapshot) has no coordinates and predates the 2023 census anchor; the only current geocoded alternatives found (healthsites.io, HOTOSM) are OpenStreetMap-derived, not official, and self-disclose incomplete coverage. The ward population denominator is also not yet in the canonical registry. No county or constituency value is inherited downward.

data/p23x/health-facility-child-domain-review.json identifies the live Ministry of Health KMHFR registry (which exposes constituency and ward fields) as a genuine 'direct_official_aggregation_candidate' for an independently versioned current facility-stock series, distinct from the 2023 census-assessed count. That materialization has not yet been performed: it requires a reproducible dated registry snapshot plus verified operational-status, duplicate and geography-reconciliation controls before publication, none of which has been built or run in this session. Publishing an unaudited scrape now would risk exactly the kind of unverified duplicate/closed-facility inclusion the review's prohibited-methods list rules out, so this indicator remains governed_unavailable pending that pipeline rather than being force-promoted.

As at constituency level, KMHFR is a genuine ward-level aggregation candidate per data/p23x/health-facility-child-domain-review.json, but no reproducible dated snapshot with verified status/duplicate/geography controls has been built or run in this session, so no ward value can be defensibly published yet.

The Atlas's governed source for this indicator is Table 4a of KNBS's 2013 Statistical Abstract, which publishes 2009 census population by county only (the 47 county values reconcile exactly to the published national total). A separate 2009-census constituency table exists in different, superseded KNBS volumes, but it reflects the pre-2012 210-constituency configuration; the 2012 boundary-delimitation exercise redrew constituencies rather than simply subdividing them, and no authoritative crosswalk from the 210-constituency 2009 configuration to the current 290 constituencies is published. Neither the governed county source nor the superseded constituency table can be used to populate the current 290-constituency geography without fabricating a correspondence the source does not establish.

The governed county source for this indicator (2013 Statistical Abstract Table 4a) does not reach constituency level (see the constituency-level closure for this indicator), and county assembly wards did not exist as a delimited geography at the time of the 2009 census, so no ward-domain 2009 population figure or crosswalk can exist.

See data/p23/constituency-census-closure-contract.json, which already closes this indicator at constituency level; this entry brings that closure into the P23X cascade ledger.

See data/p24/ward-census-closure-contract.json.

The canonical value is KNBS's Kenya Poverty Report 2022, based on the Kenya Continuous Household Survey (KCHS). The KCHS sample design supports exactly 50 estimation domains — national, urban, rural and the 47 counties — and does not include constituency as an estimation domain; the report's Table 4.4 / Annex Table E.2 publishes county estimates with standard errors only. Producing a constituency figure would require either an unsupported small-area model outside this design or copying the county rate downward, both of which the cascade contract prohibits.

The KCHS sample design's 50 estimation domains (national, urban, rural, 47 counties) do not include constituency or ward; since the survey does not support even a constituency-domain estimate (see the constituency-level closure), it self-evidently cannot support a ward-domain estimate.
